title: On‑Prem Runtime Protection and Rollback Checklist
author: Aisha Thompson
body:
Overview
--------
This document is a compact, operator-focused checklist and playbook for protecting the on‑prem runtime during upgrades, handling failed rollouts, and performing safe rollbacks. It covers preflight validations, controlled rollout patterns, concrete automated checks, rollback decision thresholds, and post‑rollback remediation. It is intended for field engineers, SREs, and operator teams responsible for Redwood Private installs.

Scope
-----
- Applies to Redwood Private on‑prem and VPC deploys where rwd-runtime and rwd-operator components are installed.
- Covers: preflight checks, compatibility verification, canary/percentage rollouts, rollback decision criteria, safe-state snapshots, remediation steps.
- Does NOT replace customer‑specific compliance work — treat this as an operational baseline.

Goals and SLO implications
-------------------------
- Maintain availability SLO: 99.9% per-tenant during upgrade windows (operator target).
- Latency guardrail: P95 response time increase <= 20% from baseline; P95 absolute cap 250ms for inference control plane calls.
- Error budget threshold for rollback: any canary cohort error rate > 1.0% OR increase in 5xxs by 3x over baseline for >10m triggers rollback evaluation.

Ownership and contacts
----------------------
- Primary owner_team: engineering (eng-private-deployments & eng-serving-runtime).
- Oncall escalation: private-deploys-oncall@redwood.internal
- Field lead (example): Aisha Thompson (author), Marco Li (SRE reviewer).

Preflight verification (before pushing any runtime change)
--------------------------------------------------------
1) Baseline capture (automated):
   - Snapshot current metrics: 5xx rate, success p95/p99, tokens/sec, and average GPU utilization per node.
   - Capture current KV-cache hit rate and prefix-cache size.
   - Command (example):
```
rwdctl metrics snapshot --namespace tenant-alpha --out baseline-2026-02-15.json
```

2) Binary/package integrity and signature checks:
   - Ensure image signature valid and digest matches release manifest.
   - Command: `rwdctl image verify --image rwd-runtime:2026-02-14`

3) Hardware/firmware and attestation:
   - Verify TPM/HSM attestations and firmware versions against allowed list.
   - Minimum GPU firmware rev: NVIDIA 55.12 or later (field-specific).

4) Config compatibility matrix (quick table):
| Component | Minimum supported version | Config items to verify |
| rwd-runtime | 2.4.0 | kv_cache.max_entries, tokenizer_hash |
| rwd-operator | 1.8.0 | rollout_strategy, health_probe.path |
| rwd-upgrade-agent | 0.9.3 | snapshot_location, disk_quota |

5) Resource validation:
   - Confirm available GPU headroom for canary pool (minimum 5% of cluster capacity).
   - Check node disk free >= 10GB for snapshot storage.

Controlled rollout pattern (recommended)
---------------------------------------
1) Canary cohort (static): 1% of traffic (minimum 2 replicas) for 15 minutes.
2) Canary cohort (time box): Observe health and metrics for 15–30 minutes. Use automated gates (see gating rules).
3) Staged ramps: 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with 15–30m observation windows.
4) Automated pause on gate fail, manual approval required before further ramp.

Gating rules (automated)
------------------------
- Abort and rollback if any of the following within an observation window:
  - Error rate (5xx) in canary cohort > 1.0% absolute.
  - Error rate increases > 3x relative to baseline.
  - Latency P95 increase > 40% relative to baseline OR P95 exceeds 400ms.
  - Model output degradation detected by quality hooks (see Eval hook below).

Quality hooks and lightweight evals
----------------------------------
- Run a small prompt set of 50 representative prompts (golden set) against canary. Compare embedding/text generation differences using automatic diff thresholds.
- Example command: `rwdctl eval run --suite canary-golden-50 --target canary-123`
- If quality delta > 2% (metric: token-level perplexity proxy or task-specific accuracy), pause rollout and trigger manual inspection.

Rollback decision matrix (quick reference)
-----------------------------------------
- Immediate rollback (automated): gate violation (see above) OR critical runtime crash affecting >5% nodes.
- Conditional rollback (operator judgment): slow but steady increase in errors over 30m or customer‑reported incorrect outputs.
- Manual rollback (last resort): data corruption, KV-state divergence, or compliance-triggered rollback.

Rollback procedure (step-by-step)
--------------------------------
1) Put system into read-only or degraded-safe mode (if supported): `rwdctl cluster set-mode --mode degraded-safe`
2) Stop new version rollout and scale canary replicas to 0: `rwdctl rollout abort --release rwd-runtime:2026-02-15`
3) Trigger rollback of runtime binary to previous known-good digest: `rwdctl image roll back --component rwd-runtime --to-digest sha256:abcd1234`
4) Restore runtime state snapshot (see safe-state snapshot section).
5) Validate post-rollback baseline: run the same baseline snapshot and golden evals.
6) Lift degraded-safe mode and resume traffic: `rwdctl cluster set-mode --mode normal`

Safe‑state snapshots and state recovery
--------------------------------------
- Always create a safe-state snapshot before canary start. Snapshot includes: operator metadata, KV-cache exports, model index pointers, and runtime in-memory checkpoint where available.
- Snapshot command example:
```
rwdctl snapshot create --namespace tenant-alpha --include kv,operator-meta --out snapshot-2026-02-15.tar.gz
```
- Retention: keep last 5 snapshots per tenant while performing upgrades. Store snapshots to a write-once location with checksum.

Operator checklist for rollback (quick)
--------------------------------------
- [ ] Confirm snapshot exists and verified checksum.
- [ ] Abort active rollout and scale down canaries.
- [ ] Trigger image rollback to approved digest.
- [ ] Restore snapshot and confirm KV-cache consistency.
- [ ] Run golden evals and smoke tests.
- [ ] Notify customers and update incident tracker.

Post‑rollback remediation and RCA cadence
----------------------------------------
- After rollback, capture a dedicated RCA within 72 hours. RCA should include:
  - Timeline of events, metric graphs (baseline vs canary), logs from rwd-runtime and rwd-operator, eval diffs, and root cause hypothesis.
- Remediation timeline: critical fixes must be delivered to regression branch within 5 business days.

Testing and automation snippets
-----------------------------
- Example YAML for a rollout policy (rwd-operator config):
```
rolloutStrategy:
  kind: staged
  stages:
    - percent: 1
      duration: 15m
    - percent: 5
      duration: 20m
    - percent: 25
      duration: 30m
    - percent: 100
      duration: 0m
  autoPauseOnFailure: true
  failureThresholds:
    errorRateAbsolute: 0.01
    errorRateMultiplier: 3.0
    latencyP95IncreasePct: 40
```
- Health probe example (rwd-runtime container):
```
/healthz?probe=deep
```
- Automated gate-run command (CI job):
```
rwdctl rollout start --policy-file rollout-policy.yaml --dry-run=false --namespace tenant-alpha
```

Monitoring and observability hooks
---------------------------------
- Ensure microsecond‑resolution tracing is enabled for control‑plane calls: span sampling 100% for canary cohort, 10% cluster-wide.
- Key dashboards to watch during rollout:
  - "Private Deploy: Canary Metrics" (error rate, P95, KV hit rate)
  - "KV Cache Drift" (size, evictions)
  - "Model Swap Latency" (cold-starts, model load time)

Escalation and communication
---------------------------
- If rollback is executed, post an update to #private-deploys channel with: brief reason, snapshot id, rollback digest, and customer impact summary.
- Notify Customer Success for any customer-facing communication templates.

Appendix A — Fast checks and commands (cheat sheet)
--------------------------------------------------
- Verify signature: `rwdctl image verify --image rwd-runtime:2026-02-14`
- Snapshot create: `rwdctl snapshot create --namespace tenant-alpha --include kv,operator-meta`
- Start canary rollout: `rwdctl rollout start --policy-file rollout-policy.yaml`
- Abort rollout: `rwdctl rollout abort --release <release-id>`

Appendix B — Example incident log template
------------------------------------------
- Incident ID: PRV-2026-02-15-01
- Start time: 2026-02-15T10:12:00Z
- Release: rwd-runtime:2026-02-15 (sha256:abcd1234)
- Canary cohort: tenant-alpha (1% traffic)
- Trigger: 5xx spike to 2.3% at 10:22Z
- Action: Automated abort + rollback to sha256:ffef5678 started at 10:25Z
- Resolution: Rollback completed, service back to normal at 10:34Z

Related documents and references
-------------------------------
- Ephemeral Boot & Attestation Playbook (onprem) — refer to hardware attestation steps for preflight.
- Incremental Stateful Upgrade Strategy — for stateful migration considerations.

Feedback and continuous improvement
-----------------------------------
- If you discover gaps in the checklist or need additional automations, add a follow-up ticket in the eng-private-deployments backlog (label: onprem-ops).

End of document
